core_themes.name: National skills shortages and productivity
core_themes.claim: The manifesto commitment to three million apprenticeships is driven by the need to address national skill shortages and stimulate economic growth and productivity.

core_themes.name: Public sector apprenticeship gap
core_themes.claim: The public sector lags behind the private sector in apprenticeship uptake and has been asked to achieve a greater proportion of growth to close this gap.

core_themes.name: Civil Service diversity and inclusivity shortfall
core_themes.claim: Despite being the most diverse it has ever been, the Civil Service still lacks true representation and inclusivity, limiting social mobility.

core_themes.name: Disability employment gap
core_themes.claim: Disabled groups, such as those with autism, face a significant employment challenge that apprenticeships and wider policy must address.

core_themes.name: Numerical apprenticeship target
core_themes.claim: The Civil Service will deliver at least 30,000 apprenticeship starts by 2020, equating to 2.3% of the workforce annually, to lead by example in the public sector.

core_themes.name: Workforce capability and skills development
core_themes.claim: Apprenticeships will build the capability of the Civil Service workforce, filling existing and future skills gaps through transferable and profession-specific skills.

core_themes.name: Diversity and social mobility
core_themes.claim: Apprenticeships provide an opportunity to improve diversity, inclusivity and social mobility by opening entry routes to people from all backgrounds regardless of educational attainment.

core_themes.name: Economic and business case
core_themes.claim: Apprenticeships make business sense, evidenced by employer and apprentice reports of increased productivity and significant lifetime earnings returns for apprentices.

core_themes.name: Leading the wider Government apprenticeship agenda
core_themes.claim: The Civil Service Apprenticeship Programme should lead by example and align with the Government's wider apprenticeship strategy, including the levy and NAO recommendations on quality versus quantity.

core_themes.name: Quality over quantity
core_themes.claim: The programme is designed to ensure quality and parity of esteem for apprenticeships, not just to hit numerical targets.

core_themes.name: Routes to creating apprenticeships
core_themes.claim: The Civil Service will create apprenticeships through three main routes: converting external recruitment, retraining existing staff, and enhancing current schemes.

core_themes.name: Recruitment and reward reform
core_themes.claim: Successful delivery requires rethinking apprenticeship pay structures and recruitment/selection processes to focus on potential rather than the finished product.

core_themes.name: Embedding apprenticeships in career pathways
core_themes.claim: Apprenticeships will be embedded into professional career ladders, functional plans and talent management strategies to provide a viable route into and up through the Civil Service.

core_themes.name: Governance and departmental delivery structure
core_themes.claim: The Cabinet Office will set strategic direction and support departments, who will be responsible for delivering the numbers and quality of apprenticeships in their workforce plans.

core_themes.name: Devolved administration and UK-wide coverage
core_themes.claim: The strategy applies across the UK Home Civil Service, with the Cabinet Office engaging Devolved Administrations to ensure similar growth and access outside England.

core_themes.name: Targeting underrepresented groups
core_themes.claim: Implementation will include targeted outreach, recruitment and marketing to promote apprenticeships to those from lower socio-economic backgrounds and other underrepresented groups.

core_themes.name: Measurement and monitoring framework
core_themes.claim: Success will be tracked through data collection, long-term tracking of apprentice outcomes, and a set of interim goals and measures across five strategic areas.
